column1: The compiling of dictionaries has been historically the provenance of studious professorial types – usually bespectacled – who love to pore over weighty tomes and make pronouncements on the finer nuances of meaning.
column2: 词典的编纂历来是沉静学者——通常戴眼镜的教授——热衷于翻阅厚重典籍并对语言意义的细微差别发表评论的领域。

column1: They were probably good at crosswords and definitely knew a lot of words, but the image was always rather dry and dusty.
column2: 他们可能很擅长解字谜，而且肯定掌握了很多单词。不过，那些图片总是显得相当枯燥且缺乏生气。

column1: The latest technology, and simple technology at that, is revolutionising the content of dictionaries and the way they are put together.
column2: 最新的技术，甚至是相当简单的技术，正在彻底改变词典的内容及其编排方式。

column1: For the first time, dictionary publishers are incorporating real, spoken English into their data.
column2: 首次，词典出版商将真实的口语英语纳入其数据中。

column1: It gives lexicographers (people who write dictionaries) access to a more vibrant, up-to-date vernacular language which has never really been studied before.
column2: 这使得词典编纂者能够接触到一种更加丰富、最新的方言语言，而这种语言之前从未被充分研究过。

column1: In one project, 150 volunteers each agreed to discreetly tie a Walkman recorder to their waist and leave it running for anything up to two weeks.
column2: 在一个项目中，有150名志愿者同意将随身听设备隐蔽地挂在腰带上，并让设备持续运行长达两周时间。

column1: Every conversation they had was recorded.
column2: 他们每一场对话都被记录下来。

column1: When the data was collected, the length of tapes was 35 times the depth of the Atlantic Ocean.
column2: 在数据收集时，磁带的长度是大西洋深度的35倍。

column1: Teams of audio typists transcribed the tapes to produce a computerised database of ten million words.
column2: 一组音频打字员将录音带转写成一个包含一千万个单词的计算机化数据库。

column1: This has been the basis – along with an existing written corpus – for the Language Activator dictionary, described by lexicographer Professor Randolph Quirk as “the book the world has been waiting for”.
column2: 这一基础，加上已有的书面语料库，构成了《语言激活词典》的依据，辞典编纂者兰道夫·奎克教授将其形容为‘世界久等的书籍’。

column1: It shows advanced foreign learners of English how the language is really used.
column2: 这可以帮助那些正在学习英语的外国学习者了解英语在实际使用中的真实情况。

column1: In the dictionary, key words such as “eat” are followed by related phrases such as “wolf down” or “be a picky eater”, allowing the student to choose the appropriate phrase.
column2: 在词典中，像‘吃’这样的关键词后面会跟着一些相关的短语，比如‘狼吞虎咽’或‘挑食’，学生可以选择最合适的短语来表达自己的意思。

column1: “This kind of research would be impossible without computers,” said Delia Summers, a director of dictionaries.
column2: “没有计算机，这种研究根本不可能进行。”

column1: “It has transformed the way lexicographers work.
column2: 它改变了词典编纂者的工作方式。

column1: If you look at the word “like”, you may intuitively think that the first and most frequent meaning is the verb, as in “I like swimming”.
column2: 如果你看到单词‘like’，你可能会本能地认为它的第一个也是最常见的意思就是动词，比如‘我喜欢游泳’。

column1: It is not.
column2: 不是。

column1: It is the preposition, as in: “she walked like a duck”.
column2: 这就是介词的用法，比如：‘她走路的样子就像只鸭子。’

column1: Just because a word or phrase is used doesn’t mean it ends up in a dictionary.
column2: 仅仅因为一个词或短语被使用在语言中，并不意味着它最终会被收录进字典里。

column1: The sifting out process is as vital as ever.
column2: 筛选过程依然至关重要。

column1: But the database does allow lexicographers to search for a word and find out how frequently it is used – something that could only be guessed at intuitively before.
column2: 不过，这个数据库确实允许词典编纂者搜索某个单词，并了解该单词的使用频率——这在以前是无法通过直觉来推测的。

column1: Researchers have found that written English works in a very different way to spoken English.
column2: 研究人员发现，书面英语的运作方式与口语英语截然不同。

column1: The phrase “say what you like” literally means “feel free to say anything you want”, but in reality it is used, evidence shows, by someone to prevent the other person voicing disagreement.
column2: ‘说你想要的’字面意思是‘你可以自由地说任何你想说的话’，但事实上，证据显示，这种说法常被用来阻止对方表达异议。

column1: The phrase “it”s a question of crops up on the database over and over again.
column2: 在数据库中，这个短语‘它’出现了很多次。

column1: It has nothing to do with enquiry, but it’s one of the most frequent English phrases which has never been in a language learner’s dictionary before: it is now.
column2: 这与‘询问’无关，但这是最常用的英语短语之一，在语言学习者的词典中却从未出现过：就是现在。

column1: The Spoken Corpus computer shows how inventive and humorous people are when they are using language by twisting familiar phrases for effect.
column2: ‘Spoken Corpus’电脑程序展示了人们在使用语言时，如何通过扭曲熟悉短语来展现创造力和幽默感。

column1: It also reveals the power of the pauses and noises we use to play for time, convey emotion, doubt and irony.
column2: 它也揭示了我们用来营造时间感、表达情感、表达怀疑以及制造讽刺效果的停顿与音效所拥有的力量。

column1: For the moment, those benefiting most from the Spoken Corpus are foreign learners.
column2: 目前，从‘口语语料库’中获益最多的是那些学习外语的人。

column1: “Computers allow lexicographers to search quickly through more examples of real English,” said Professor Geoffrey Leech of Lancaster University.
column2: 兰卡斯特大学的杰弗里·利奇教授表示，电脑让辞典编纂者能够快速搜寻到真实的英语实例。

column1: “They allow dictionaries to be more accurate and give a feel for how language is being used.”
column2: 它们使得词典更加准确，并让人感受到语言的实际使用方式。

column1: The Spoken Corpus is part of the larger British National Corpus, an initiative carried out by several groups involved in the production of language learning materials: publishers, universities and the British Library.
column2: ‘Spoken Corpus’是‘British National Corpus’项目的一部分，该项目由多家参与语言学习材料制作的机构——出版社、大学和英国图书馆——共同协作完成。
